question: Why does adsorption of surfactants tend to occur on inner surfaces of double-layer graphene compared to outer surfaces?
answer: The adsorption of surfactants tends to occur on the inner surfaces of double-layer graphene rather than the outer surfaces due to dehydration effects between the graphene layers. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the confined space between the layers promotes stronger hydrophilic interactions among surfactant molecules, enhancing adsorption. In contrast, outer surfaces lack this confined environment, leading to weaker adsorption. Additionally, hydrophobic tail groups of surfactants exhibit stronger adsorption on graphene than hydrophilic head groups, further stabilizing the inner-layer adsorption. This behavior is consistent across simulations, demonstrating that the unique interlayer conditions in double-layer graphene favor surfactant accumulation internally.
